A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. All 33 pages of v1 and 39 pages of v2, including appendices A–G and A–H respectively, support comparison; extraction ambiguities were checked against rendered pages.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendix G report original MNIST and synthetic multiclass classification experiments, with outcomes in Figures 1–2.

after.justification: Appendix H reports the multiclass experiments and new synthetic multilabel classification results, displayed in Figures 1–3.

M1.justification: Appendix G introduces variable-delay procedures combining SOLID with OGD and the existing gradient estimators, including a feedback-arrival update procedure in Algorithm 3. Section 5.1 also changes exploration from q = B sqrt(DK/T) to B sqrt(K/T). The non-delayed estimators themselves are retained.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates only multiclass classification. v2 retains MNIST and the synthetic multiclass scenarios and adds fixed-cardinality multilabel classification in Appendix H.2, substantially extending empirical coverage to structured outputs.

E2.justification: Appendix H.2 adds a direct comparison between the inverse-weighted and pseudo-inverse estimators. The existing multiclass figures retain Gappletron with logistic loss and Gaptron with hinge and logistic losses; inconsistent setup prose does not establish a switch in those plotted comparators.

E3.justification: The new multilabel protocol uses T = 10,000, feature dimension 50, exactly five positive labels, and label dimensions 10, 12, 16, 20 and 24. It uses projected OGD with B = 50, whereas the retained multiclass protocol still specifies unprojected OGD with B = 10.

E4.justification: Appendix H.2 adds a targeted estimator comparison across label dimensions to examine when avoiding explicit output-cardinality dependence helps. The earlier multiclass sweeps over class count, feature dimension and label noise remain.

E5.justification: v2 specifies 10 repetitions for the new multilabel experiment; the retained multiclass experiments still specify 20. This adds a distinct repeated-run setting, without introducing confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty bands for Figure 3.

E6.justification: Figure 3 supplies the first empirical results for the pseudo-inverse method: inverse weighting performs better at d = 10 and 12, while the pseudo-inverse method performs better at d = 16, 20 and 24. Existing results also change: the proposed method's MNIST median error moves from approximately 39.2% to 36.6%, and its synthetic multiclass curves are updated.

T1.justification: Theorem 4.3 adds the horizon-independent O(D^2) alternative, and Theorem 5.1 changes the claimed bound from O(sqrt(DKT)) to O(sqrt((K+D)T)), with revised proofs. Appendix G adds variable-delay theorems and proofs. Assumption 3.6 adds an absolute inner-product bound, and input/output norm definitions are revised. The new delayed-bandit proof contains an unresolved expected-maximum step.

C1.justification: v2 strengthens the headline fixed-delay guarantees and promotes variable delays from future work to an addressed setting. It withdraws v1's assertion of optimal sqrt(T) dependence for bandit feedback and adds a claim of empirical support for the pseudo-inverse approach on multilabel problems.

C2.justification: v2 explains that the cited lower bound concerns graph feedback and does not establish bandit tightness, substantially revising the limitations discussion. It also adds the label-flipping qualification for multilabel cases with m > d/2 and interprets the new estimator crossover as support for the theoretical tradeoff.

D1.justification: Appendix H.2 documents Scikit-learn's make_multilabel_classification generator, repeated filtering to obtain exactly m positive labels, and the new projected-OGD settings. Existing hardware, Python/OS information and multiclass implementation details are retained.

R1.justification: The literature base is largely retained, with a Scikit-learn citation added. v2 clarifies its relationship to the graph-feedback lower bound and adds an explicit distinction between Delaytron's multiclass setting and its broader structured-prediction setting.

P1.justification: The abstract, contributions, problem description and conclusion are extensively rewritten and condensed. All experiments are consolidated into Appendix H, a variable-delay appendix is inserted, and main-text high-probability theorems become brief summaries with appendix references. Terminology and citation formatting are revised throughout.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figure 3 and Algorithm 3, expands the notation table, relocates the MNIST plot to the appendix, and resizes/reformats the retained plots. These are limited display changes within the retained single-column layout; numerical plot updates are assessed separately under E6.

improvement.justification: v2 improves the lower-bound qualification, makes an estimator assumption explicit, and adds multilabel evidence. However, Appendix F.2, Eq. (19), controls the expected maximum retained in Eq. (16) using only individual conditional-mean bounds, which do not justify that step; v1 instead used a second-moment bound. This gap affects a headline strengthened guarantee. The benefits and unresolved theoretical reliability therefore prevent a confident net quality judgment.
